card.name: Archaic poetry and old-style verse
card.fires_on: Words inside old-fashioned poems or archaic prose, often a small word or a word piece mid-line in verse. Typical settings are Victorian or medieval verse with thee, thy, and inverted word order.

modes.label: Poetic line words
modes.description: Short function or adjective words in the middle of a verse line in older poetry.
modes.example: Grown chill through something being away,<< though>> what It knows not.

modes.label: Partway through a word in verse
modes.description: A word piece inside a longer or archaic word in poetry or old text.
modes.example: And when I heard my father's language first From alien lips which had no kiss for mine, I wept aloud, then laughed, then we<<pt>>, then wept, — And

modes.label: Archaic prose
modes.description: A word in old-style historical or translated text with archaic phrasing.
modes.example: to come with a<< foreign>> people to make war on shine own

card.writes: It promotes archaic or literary words such as lore, anon, wrought and strife, which fit old-style verse.
card.plain: It marks words in old-fashioned poetry and archaic writing, far from drug-label text.
